ety.text: Borrowed from French théâtre, from Latin theātrum, from Ancient Greek θέατρον (théatron) (a verbal noun of θεάομαι (theáomai)). Displaced феа́тр (feátr), which had been borrowed from the Medieval Greek. Compare natively formed Czech divadlo (i.e **дива́ло, akin to диви́ться (divítʹsja)); Serbo-Croatian позориште (akin to позо́рище (pozórišče) (the meaning theater in Russian is obsolete)), Serbo-Croatian казалиште (i.e. **каза́лище, akin to показа́ть (pokazátʹ)), Slovene gledališče (i.e. **гляда́лище, akin to гляде́ть (gljadétʹ)).

s.g: Troitsky (referring to anyone with this last name, or to anything named after such a person)
